reviews.author: Christy S.
reviews.text:
Great staff! We reserved 2 tent sites, unseen in person,(online photos), with power/ water. We arrived on a Monday, with the following Thursday as our departure day.
Unfortunately the weather decided to give us a challenge as it rained hard on Monday, we checked in and got directions to our sites. We pull up and discover that it had(&would continue for another 18 hours) to pour down rain.. like big heavy rain drops!
Both our sites were flooded.. like ankle deep water, small lakes exactly where our tents were supposed to go.. the only place they could be set up actually. I found all the tent sights to be on the small size. A larger tent(like anything that sleeps more than 4 would not fit any sites here.. unless set up on the pavement.  Then you can't anchor it down.)
Anyway, so back to the office and advised of the flooded sites. The ranger took a map and searched thru his computer until he found a selection of available sites next to each other for our reservation requirements to choose from. He said go drive the loops and look at the sites once we found the two that would work for us to come back and he got them switched for us.
The next day the rain wasn't as bad and the mosquitoes started looking for their food..aka us!
Make sure to bring bug spray or better still.. use the premithin spray that  lasts 6 weeks or 6 laundry washing on your tents, clothing, shoes, ect. Do not spray it on ur clothes while wearing ur clothes.. follow directions! We had 40% deer and it slowed them down a little.. not much. We also had the thermocell misting machine mosquitoe repellent  and 2 large costco brand citronella candles and finally the bug repellent sticks that you light, stick in the ground around ur site and it slowly burns.. we still got attacked by the mosquitoes  so be aware that there is an issue with the mosquitoes here!
Everywhere but the actual beach where the wind seems to keep them away.
Otherwise, all the attractions at the park are great. The rv sites Great, staff, awesome, plenty of hot water for showers.
Have fun in town lots of shops, attractions to do locally.

reviews.author: Carl O.
reviews.text: Fun riding the trails. Bathrooms/showers were a little rough but lots of hot water. Came during fishing season, wouldn't suggest it unless you are fishing too. Loop E has showers.

reviews.author: JoAnn D.
reviews.text:
Beautiful escape from city-life, just a few miles out. Quiet, peaceful, and easy to navigate.

Nice pull through available for bigger rigs.

$10 to dump, electric and water at the sites.

Elk roaming freely throughout the park, drive slowly and cautiously.

Restrooms close by, firepits and picnic tables all around.

This site shown is Loop F, #235.

reviews.author: Cathy O.
reviews.text: Wonderful campground! Basic/clean/free hot showers. Paved bike paths, playgrounds, hiking trails. We had a nice, relatively private site : 236 F. Not perfectly level but worked fine. Laundromat just outside the park.

reviews.author: Hal K.
reviews.text:
Very nice campground that is well laid out. Close to a lot of different things to do. We used it as a base to explore the area South to Tillamook and over to Astoria, and also to the Washington side of Fort Canby. We especially liked Astoria with the Sunday market and the Astoria column at sunset.
One of the few negatives is the presence of mosquitoes near our campsite on h loop must be pretty boggy in the middle and nearby
The other negative is the cost of the sites with the addition of of fees I.e daily fees and markup for non-residents. This is not a cheap campground to stay at. But relative to the KOA across the street, it's still cheaper.
